title: 2026-11-04_Cryptocurrency_Miner_Investigation_7b6
description: Security monitoring has detected unusual CPU usage and network activity on a compromised host. Your task is to investigate the system, identify the malicious activity, and determine how it was deployed and spread across the network.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: Security monitoring has detected unusual CPU usage and network activity on a compromised host. Your task is to investigate the system, identify the malicious activity, and determine how it was deployed and spread across the network.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content: Connect to the miner-host using SSH with the provided credentials. Username: trainee, Password: trainee. Enter 'start' to begin.
levels.local_content: Local sandbox access is not required for this scenario. Connect to the miner-host using SSH with the provided credentials. Username: trainee, Password: trainee. Enter 'start' to begin.

levels.title: Identify Suspicious Service
levels.content: Security monitoring has detected an unusual CPU-intensive and network-facing component on the compromised host. Investigate the running services and identify the service responsible for the suspicious activity.
levels.solution:
1. Connect to the miner-host using SSH with the provided credentials.
2. List all running services using the command `systemctl list-units --type=service --state=running`.
3. Identify the service with an unusual name or description.
4. Check the status of the suspicious service using `systemctl status <service>`.
5. Note the service name for the hidden flag.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Use `systemctl list-units --type=service --state=running` to list all running services.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for services with unusual names or descriptions that do not match typical system services.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Use `systemctl status <service>` to check the status and details of a suspicious service.

levels.title: Determine Network Port
levels.content: An unfamiliar network service appears to be involved in unauthorized communication with an external system. Investigate the service and determine the network port associated with this communication.
levels.solution:
1. From the miner-host, investigate the suspicious service identified in the previous task.
2. Use `systemctl cat <service>` to view the service configuration file.
3. Look for the `ExecStart` line, which specifies the path to the script launched by the service.
4. Inspect the script using `cat <script>` to find the port number used for communication.
5. Note the port number for the hidden flag.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for the `ExecStart` line in the service configuration file to find the script path.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Use `cat <script>` to inspect the script and find the port number used for communication.

levels.title: Identify Persistence Mechanism
levels.content: Investigators suspect that a mechanism keeps the miner service running across reboots and process termination. Determine which system component is responsible for this activity.
levels.solution:
1. From the miner-host, investigate the suspicious service identified in the previous tasks.
2. Use `systemctl status <service>` to check the status and details of the service.
3. Look for any associated timers or cron jobs that might be responsible for persistence.
4. Use `grep -Rni . /etc/cron.d/ 2>/dev/null` to search for cron jobs related to the service.
5. Note the cron job name for the hidden flag.
